title: The metric Blaschke theorem
main_claim: Every closed Riemannian manifold with inj = diam is, up to scale, a CROSS. Proof: (A) a sharp lower bound Vol(M) >= Vol(model) at equal diameter, from a fixed-chart Schur-complement split of the Jacobi determinant plus Kazdan's weighted Jensen cancellation, with equality giving harmonic, hence CROSS by Szabo; (B) matching upper bounds: CP^r via Yang 1991, HP^2/OP^2 via Kramer–Stolz plus the Reznikov volume theorem as recorded by Wilking, and HP^r (r>=2) via an intrinsic argument (incidence Pontryagin class, signature forcing s=1, Gysin lattice of the geodesic space, first free-loop negative bundle, complete-intersection bound N <= C(4r,2r)/(2r+1)).

issues.description: The Cayley-plane upper volume bound rests entirely on a secondary attribution: Wilking 2001, p.282, crediting Reznikov with an equal-volume theorem for Zoll manifolds homeomorphic to a CROSS. No primary source for the OP^2 case is cited (the cited Reznikov papers cover HP^n and CP^n), and the intrinsic quaternionic argument is not extended to OP^2. This is not a logical gap in the paper's own reasoning, but a reader would need to confirm that the cited statement really covers OP^2.
issues.evidence: Proof of Cor. rig:planes: 'the Riemannian weak Blaschke volume theorem recorded by Wilking and attributed there to Reznikov applies ... [Wilking2001, p.282]'. The bibliography has only Reznikov1985HP and Reznikov1994CP.

coverage: Read all sections 00–09 in full. Checked line by line: Lagrangian graph chart and pole expansions (residue only in the k-block, H smooth through D); the Schur bounds Q >= ∫S in all four folded index cases, including the reversed order (1,0) and the cut-pair zeros Q(u,u+D)=0 from nullity k; the Minkowski determinant-root inequality; the weighted scalar identity (recomputed F'(t) and F = I_W sin^2/(2λ)); the folded weight matrix row/column sums; the global Fubini/flow-invariance step giving V >= V0. As a numerical sanity check of the comparison, I tested reparametrized model Lagrangian loops: the ratio stayed >= 1 for (m,k) = (2,1), (4,3), (8,7), (6,1). Quaternionic part: checked Prop inc:normal (the half-spin integrality argument giving t ≡ 2 mod 4), the rank-constraint algebra (top coefficient a_{r-2}^2 - a_{r-3}a_{r-1} = 1), and computed the signature numerically for s = 1, 3, 5 and r = 2..12 (s=1 gives 1,0,1,0,...; s>=3 gives (-1)^r σ >> 1, consistent with the contour estimate). Gysin lattice and middle determinant r+1, the relations Q=R=0 from x^{r+1}=0 and the antipode, and the complete-intersection Hilbert series all check out. In sympy I verified the determinant formula det(J_{i+j}) = ±(r+1)(4α)^{-r(r-1)/2} for r = 2,3,4 at several (α,β), and |Φ_{-1/4,1}(X^{2r-1})| = C(4r,2r)/(2r+1). I did not independently verify the classical inputs: the Besse/McKay structure theory, Yang 1991, Kramer–Stolz, the Wilking/Reznikov statement, and the Ottosen–Bökstedt equivariant attachment framework.
